newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia stocks close lower, Foster's lifts trade.
newsitem.headline: Australia stocks close lower, Foster's lifts trade.

text.p: The Australian stock market held its head just above the 2,600 mark on Friday in a day dominated by the placement of A$1.54 billion (US$1.2 billion) of Foster's Brewing Group shares.
The All Ordinaries Index firmed off its lows in afternoon trade to close down just 3.3 points at 2,600.9, a fall of 9.6 points from the previous Friday's close.
Dealers said there appeared to be some institutional selling to fund the Foster's take-up, but less than might have been expected given the size of the placement.
"The market hasn't been hit too badly," said Simon Burge, investment manager at Tyndall Australia.
Many institutions had been sitting on cash this year and may not have needed to dispose of assets to fund the purchase, while much of the stock also went overseas, he said.
The placement of 616.6 million Foster's shares owned by the the Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd followed its long-awaited move to end an 11-year link with the brewing group.

Were Stockbroking managing director John Paterson said retail investors bought about A$150 million of the A$1.535 billion package, with overseas institutions taking 55 percent of the remainder and local institutions 45 percent.
Elsewhere, the Australia and New Zealand Banking Group (ANZ) rose 30 cents to A$9.09 on turnover of 2.19 million shares.
Dealers said appetite for ANZ may have been renewed by investors discounting a rumour on Thursday of a possible takeover bid for rival Westpac Banking Corp.
Westpac, meanwhile, confirmed it had sold a 2.99 percent stake in publishing group John Fairfax Holdings Ltd. Merrill Lynch specialled the line of 22.75 million shares at A$3.30.

Other stocks to show strong turnover included Pacific Dunlop, which eased 10 cents to A$3.64 on turnover of 15 million shares, and National Australia Bank which fell 11 cents to A$18.77 million on turnover of 10.5 million.
